definition: Parameters are learned by training (weights, biases); hyperparameters are set by the practitioner (learning rate, batch size, layer count, LoRA rank) and tuned by experimentation.
details: Parameters are learned by training (weights, biases); hyperparameters are set by the practitioner (learning rate, batch size, layer count, LoRA rank) and tuned by experimentation.

explainer.lead: Parameters are learned by training, while hyperparameters are set by the practitioner and tuned by experimentation. The distinction matters because it determines what the training process discovers versus what you must choose and search over.

tiers.eli5: A parameter is something the student learns from studying; a hyperparameter is the study schedule the teacher sets beforehand.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers let training learn weights and biases while choosing learning rate, batch size, layer count, or LoRA rank themselves and tuning them by experimentation. A pitfall is treating a hyperparameter as learned — no amount of training will adjust a value you fixed.
tiers.paperLevel: Parameters are learned by training (weights, biases); hyperparameters are set by the practitioner (learning rate, batch size, layer count, LoRA rank) and tuned by experimentation.

explainer.example: In a neural network, the weight matrices are parameters updated by gradient descent, while the learning rate of 0.001 and batch size of 32 are hyperparameters chosen before training.
